data.narrative:
Solugen, a Series D climate and energy company founded by Gaurab Chakrabarti and Sean Hunt, has raised over $640M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Redwood Materials at $6.0B Series D, KoBold Metals at $3.0B Series C, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B Series C, and Amogy at $700M Series C), alongside one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier to $640M, yields $960M. Peer-median analysis across the four climate/energy comparables produces a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $6.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material differences in technology maturity and commercial stage within the cohort.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $816M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.5B. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer comparables—particularly Redwood Materials at comparable stage—support the higher range. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the peer set's wide valuation dispersion, the limited public market data, and the binary nature of commercialization outcomes typical in frontier climate tech.
